The [Hreflang Tag Generator](/hreflang-tag-generator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Generate hreflang tags for multilingual pages — one tag per language. Enter your URLs with language codes (one per line: URL, code) and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Generate hreflang tags for multilingual pages: enter each language version of a page with its language code, and copy the finished <link rel="alternate" hreflang="…"> tags into every version's <head>. Hreflang tells search engines which language and region each version is for, so visitors land on the right one. Use codes like en, de, fr, or en-US for a region. Everything runs in your browser; nothing is uploaded. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Hreflang Tag Generator

Start by typing or pasting your URLs with language codes (one per line: URL, code). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. List each language version: its URL and its language code, one per line.
2. Add an x-default entry for the fallback page if you have one.
3. Copy the tags and paste them into the <head> of every language version.

The fastest way to see what the [Hreflang Tag Generator](/hreflang-tag-generator) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## Language codes

Use ISO codes: en for English, de for German, fr for French, and optionally a region — en-US, en-GB, de-DE, fr-CA. x-default marks the fallback page shown when no language matches. Codes are case-sensitive in the usual form: language lowercase, region uppercase.

## The rule everyone forgets

Hreflang is reciprocal: every version of a page must link to every other version, including itself. If page A links to page B but B does not link back to A, search engines ignore the tags. Generate the full set once and paste the same set into every version.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Every version must link to every version, including itself.
- Use x-default for the page visitors see when no language matches.
- Check the result with the hreflang testing tool in Search Console.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is hreflang?

An HTML tag that tells search engines a page has versions in different languages or for different regions, so the right version shows in each country's results. Try it with your own numbers in the [Hreflang Tag Generator](/hreflang-tag-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What language codes do I use?

ISO codes such as en, de, fr — with an optional region, en-US or en-GB. x-default marks the fallback page. Try it with your own numbers in the [Hreflang Tag Generator](/hreflang-tag-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Do the tags go on every version?

Yes. Each version of a page must carry the full set of tags, including a tag pointing at itself. One-way links are ignored. Try it with your own numbers in the [Hreflang Tag Generator](/hreflang-tag-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What do I need to use the Hreflang Tag Generator?

Just URLs with language codes (one per line: URL, code). Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
